chapter_theme: The divisions of the cosmic eggs (அண்டாதி பேதம்): the world-spheres are as many as the sands of the seven seas, all under the Lord seated on them, and the tattvas spread through them in fixed multiples.

2297.reading: The outer cosmic egg and the eggs divided within it, as many as the grains of sand of the seven wave-tossed seas, shine like sparks of light and gold ornaments, and the Lord of the gods sits on them as his seat.
2297.nuance: பகிரண்டம் is the outer egg enclosing the worlds. அண்டாசனம் (the egg as seat) is taken here as the Lord enthroned over the cosmos; the sand of the seas is a conventional figure for numberless worlds.

2298.reading: Above the cosmic mountain the bliss tattva, with five bodies, pervades as the thirty-six; the endless tattvas it becomes are eightfold in the flawless egg.
2298.nuance: ஆனந்த தத்துவம், அண்டாசலம் (cosmic mountain, or perhaps அண்டாசனம் again), the five bodies and the eightfold multiple are cosmological terms the verse doesn't explain.

source_issues: 2298: line 2 reads பத்தாறாய்க், with a stray க் before தான்.

links.note: 2297 says the cosmic eggs are as many as the sand of the seven seas (எறிகடல் ஏழின் மணல்அளவாக) and the Lord sits on them as his seat; 1149 praises Shakti who shapes the countless eggs (அண்டகோடிகள்) within. The countless eggs are the Lord's seat in one verse and Shakti's work in the other.
